text:
Samir Patel: FYI - staging hit a big spike during a shard reassignment, queues ballooned and retries piled up. seeing timeouts + 429s from the runner.
Maria Chen: ugh, seen that pattern before. any logs/trace ids?
Samir Patel: trace=tr-9923, logs: 
```
 2026-02-18T15:12:02Z runner: shard-handoff start shard=42 dst=worker-9
 2026-02-18T15:12:03Z queue: enqueue task=eval-... worker-9 len=0
 2026-02-18T15:12:03Z worker-9: accept handshake
 2026-02-18T15:12:03Z worker-9: panic process-shard: kv-cache mismatch
 2026-02-18T15:12:03Z runner: shard-handoff failed shard=42 err=panic
 2026-02-18T15:12:03Z runner: retry immediately shard=42
 2026-02-18T15:12:03Z queue: enqueue task=eval-... worker-7 len=120
 2026-02-18T15:12:04Z queue: enqueue task=eval-... worker-8 len=230
 2026-02-18T15:12:05Z runner: rate-limit hit, returning 429
```
Samir Patel: root cause looks like immediate retries + no jitter on handoff -> thundering herd across workers.
Alex Gomez: does the runner backoff? I thought we had exponential backoff on handoff failures.
Samir Patel: we do for task retries, but shard handoff path requeues immediately with no randomized delay.
Olivia Park: eval-bot alerted: "high queue depth" at 15:12:06 (incident id inc-20260218-01).
eval-bot: ALERT staging/generic-eval-runner queue_depth>200 for 3m.
Kevin Zhou: quick mitigation suggestion: add a short randomized delay + small circuit-breaker when worker error rates spike. also cap requeue additions per-second.
Maria Chen: agreed. small patch: add jittered backoff on handoff and update shard assignment logic to mark a worker unhealthy for 30s after N panics.
Alex Gomez: propose pseudocode: 
```
func attemptHandoff(shard, dst) {
  if dst.recentPanics > 3 {
    markUnhealthy(dst)
    return scheduleReassignWithDelay(shard, base=200ms, jitter=rand(0,150ms))
  }
  err := handshake(dst)
  if err != nil {
    delay := min(5s, base*(2^attempt)) + rand(0, base)
    scheduleReassignWithDelay(shard, delay)
  }
}
```
Olivia Park: can we also add a leaky-bucket on the global reassign queue so a sudden flood doesn't overload workers?
Samir Patel: yes. implement both: per-worker health window + global rate cap.
Maria Chen: CI note: we need a test that simulates simultaneous handoffs of 50 shards to the same worker to reproduce. our current unit tests only do single-handoff flows.
Kevin Zhou: I'll add an integration test in the eval-harness CI job that spins up N fake workers and injects panics to validate backoff + circuit-breaker.
Alex Gomez: also add metrics: handoff_attempts, handoff_failures, worker_unhealthy_count, reassign_rate. Grafana dashboard tile recommended.
Olivia Park: linking the staging grafana panel: https://grafana.internal/redwood/board/6?panel=handoff (watch the 15:12 window)
Samir Patel: thanks. I'll open a quick-fix PR for staging that adds jitter+cap (branch: fix/handoff-jitter-1763).
Maria Chen: txn: PR link?
Samir Patel: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pull/261 - small change, no schema changes.
eval-bot: PR 261 CI status: failing (integration-evals) - timeout on simulated load test.
Kevin Zhou: expected. I'll iterate on the test to wait for backoff behavior.
Alex Gomez: long-term: we should consider leader-based handoff coordination so only leader schedules reassigns for a shard to avoid parallel reassign churn.
Maria Chen: good idea, file a follow-up RFC? I'll draft one.
Samir Patel: TODOs: 1) merge staging hotfix once tests updated (owner: Kevin) 2) add Grafana tiles (owner: Alex) 3) RFC for leader handoff (owner: Maria) 4) postmortem if this hits prod (owner: Samir)
Olivia Park: marking as high-priority for this sprint. :white_check_mark:
Samir Patel: thanks all — will update thread when PR passes CI and we roll to staging.
